tickets.first_deliverable: Use the actual finite separator/geometry/fringe conditions to find feasible M, then extract c_M and charge binary replacement. The cited proof has necessary M >=204800, already excluding M=16/32.
tickets.notes: Source audit 2026-10-13: Theorem 1.2 uses M/32 < m <= M/16 and sqrt(2(1+ln m)/m) <= (1/5)*k^(-4). For k>=2 and integer m>=1 this implies m>=12800, hence M>=204800; the real finite threshold is larger. This is a necessary-condition hand derivation, not an improved upper bound. Do not substitute the large-M asymptotic coefficient at small M. Ideal-limit screen 2026-11-02 (model, experiments/chvatal/UB-09-IDEAL-LIMIT.md): Theorem 1.1 is this framework with Batcher m-sorters, so it is the existing binary line. With attack-level separators (C_B 0.084, attack eps_F table) Chvatal's constraints bottom out at about 300; certified C_B 0.39 gives 351. Removing the Lemma 4.2 slack term gives 221. Not a separate sub-300 route. CORRECTED 2026-11-03 (TREE-PRICING.md): the screen charged 2 sorts per step with 3-sort separator constants. At 3 sorts, the best existing analysis is about 384 at attack separators and R3 is 332, so the lever is separator stage depth at fixed leak, not the tree analysis. Stage screen 2026-11-03 (STAGE-SCREEN.md): no sort/random-scramble stage gets below about 333 (band + merge-first, attack, R2c). The round-1 tail decays like 1/W under attack, so the next lever is a round 1 with a light tail by construction (designed scramble or height cap). Designed scrambles 2026-11-07 (DESIGNED-SCRAMBLE.md): dead. For n >= m every design has a tail of at least about 0.16/W (design-independent random-target hand bound, matching the attack within 5%); designs help only at small nodes (m > n). Sub-300 is out of reach in the binary Chvatal architecture at model level.

Constants are float, not interval-certified. 2026-10-19: obligations 2-3 done (FRINGE-CERT.md, reviewed): at (64, 2^11, 2^-5), mu=(1-2^-10)2^-28, delta=1.38e-9, eps_B=2^-25, lg m=38, the fringe f=32760 at J=1.15e7 is interval-certified (new tighter R2 tail), and (4.1)-(4.5) hold in exact rationals, so the 1326 point needs only package-side conditions and Lean. tickets.notes: Bags are assembled from row slabs of just-separated (balanced) bags, so input heights are confined to a window F*W, and the round-1 tail scales with the window, not m (attack: ~0.25 D/W rows, exactly 0 for W >= D). Stage = sort, scramble, two-grid band over F*W; leak ~0.25 F^2 rows. Model price under the proved R1 tree: 191-262 for F <= 2k and leak up to 6x attack; 321+ at F = 4k. The height cap also gives exact rare-cohort capture. UPDATE 2026-11-10 (WARM-START.md section 7): the real layout gives F ~ A/nu = 2^(y+z), not k. Window-only invariant: F^2 leak confirmed by exact attack, 335 (R1) / 307 (R2c) at attack level, not sub-300. Back-to-back 20-stage chains contract to a fixed point (input sd ~0.56F) and leak 0 at X = 4F after 2 stages. Variance invariant: leak ~F/16 rows, model 284-291 (R1) / 236-250 (R2c). UPDATE 2026-11-11 (section 8): Lemma G (grouped round-2 contraction, corollary of Theorem R2) proved by hand: grouped L1 l' <~ 2CF sqrt(l), fixed point ~F^2. Tight: within the stationary L1 budget an aligned dual climb gives about 2 sqrt(F) times the random grouped L1 (3.8x, 8.3x, 17x at F = 4, 16, 64; leak 240 rows at F = 64). So per-stage invariants price in the F^2 class (335 R1 / 307 R2c at attack level); not sub-300. Parked.
